supersedes: FLEET_AN_ORPHANED_WEDGE_HOLDS_TWO_QB2_DEVICES.json, DELETED not labelled. Every claim in it about the process was wrong. It is reproduced nowhere; this file is the record.
headline: I reported a qb2 process as an orphaned wedge holding two devices with no owner and no lease. It is none of those things. It is a healthy multiprocessing spawn child of a live A/B benchmark that holds the benchlock and is correctly pinned to one card. I did not kill it -- that decision was right -- but the report was wrong and is withdrawn.

what_it_actually_is.265319: multiprocessing spawn_main child -- a worker waiting on its queue
what_it_actually_is.191952: benchlock.sh pvx-gate-land -- IT HOLDS THE BENCHLOCK
what_it_actually_is.191922: bash -c cd /home/ttuser/tt-bio-dev && CARD=2 nohup bash perf/pvx_gate_land/shipped_fold_wide_k.sh
what_it_actually_is.owner: the pvx-gate-land campaign, alive, four levels above the pid I read

the_three_errors_and_what_each_one_actua.why_wrong: I read ppid ONE generation and stopped. The parent's own ppid (264900) was printed in my very first ps line and I did not follow it. The owner was four levels up, alive the whole time. One ppid hop does not establish orphanhood; walking to init does.

the_three_errors_and_what_each_one_actua.claimed: owner is sizeladder, which has no live worker and no concluded marker
the_three_errors_and_what_each_one_actua.why_wrong: I inferred the owning campaign from a PATH IN ARGV -- `perf/size512/fixtures/` -- and `size512` is a fixture directory, not a campaign. I then searched for `worker.sh sizeladder*`, found nothing, and read that absence as CONFIRMING the orphan. It only confirmed that I had guessed the wrong owner. A search for an owner you named by guessing cannot corroborate the guess.

the_three_errors_and_what_each_one_actua.claimed: wedged: 100 % CPU in futex_do_wait, nothing written for 4.5 h
the_three_errors_and_what_each_one_actua.why_wrong: for a multiprocessing spawn child, 100 % CPU in futex_do_wait is the NORMAL shape of a worker spinning on a queue while a sibling computes -- and a 2-rung A/B flip at 1088 has long compute phases that write nothing. Both readings are what health looks like here. The recorded p300c wedge signature is not `100 % CPU in futex` on its own, and I matched on the part instead of the pattern.

the_one_claim_that_survives_but_much_wea: I said it held devices with NO LEASE, so pick_card could double-allocate. It holds no LEASE FILE, true -- but it is not unlocked: it holds the BENCHLOCK and is pinned CARD=2. The fleet has two authorities on card occupancy, not one, and reading only `state/leases/` sees half. That is a real and much smaller point than the one I filed, and it is a question for whoever owns pick_card, not an incident.
and_one_factual_correction: two fds, ONE device. `ls -l /proc/265319/fd` resolves both fd 13 and fd 14 to /dev/tenstorrent/2. I wrote `2 Tenstorrent device fds held` and then read it as two devices. Devices 0, 1 and 3 are free.
the_near_miss: had I acted on my own report I would have killed a live benchmark mid-run while it held the benchlock. The reason I did not is the reason that held up: it was not my process, so the decision was not mine. That instinct was load-bearing here in a way the evidence was not.
the_check_that_would_have_caught_it_in_o: walk the ancestry to init before writing the word orphan: `p=PID; while read pp cmd; do echo $p $cmd; p=$pp; done` -- this campaign already records `fleet-kill-outer-pid-leaves-orphan-engine`, which is the SAME tree read from the other end. I had the shape in memory and applied it only downward.
